gap: No result ChatGPT got states how TerraMaster's Thunderbolt/USB4 NAS ports connect to a computer. TerraMaster's own help page says you use a separate IP link: in TOS you assign an IP address to an interface named 'TBLAN', the computer needs a Thunderbolt 3/4/5 or full-featured USB4 port and a certified Thunderbolt cable, and the Thunderbolt IP 'may change' after either device restarts.
standout_why: I compared against the cited QNAP TVS-h674T US page, which gives a 20 Gbps 'Thunderbolt Networking' maximum and macOS 13.5 or later but no setup mechanism. I also checked QNAP's Thunderbolt solution page, which says 20Gb/s, assign an IP with Qfinder Pro, and nothing more. UGREEN's cited blog (ai.ugreen.com) already covers the IP/SMB path, the 169.254.x.x address, one computer per port, no port bonding and no disk-mode access, so none of that is new. The two support.ugnas.com guides would not render for me. No ChatGPT result included a TerraMaster page. In one chat ChatGPT recommended the $799.99 TerraMaster F6-425 Pro and told the shopper to 'verify direct Mac Thunderbolt networking support before buying', and none of its results answers that. The TerraMaster help page shows TOS has the IP-over-Thunderbolt mechanism and recommends macOS. Our current page doesn't list TerraMaster at all.
decides: Every NAS here works the same way: the Mac and NAS are both hosts, so the Mac gets an SMB share over a private IP link on the Thunderbolt cable and never sees a disk. A NAS qualifies only if its OS creates that network interface. QNAP (20 Gbps cap), UGREEN (DXP480T Plus, DXP6800 Pro and DXP8800 Plus on UGOS 1.2.0.2121 or later) and, per its help page, TerraMaster's TOS all do. Asustor's USB4 does not (our page's existing KB citation). So TerraMaster moves from 'unverified' to 'the maker says yes, but no review has measured it'. NASCompares' 16 Jul 2026 F6-425 Pro article lists the USB4 behaviour as still needing proper review testing. The pick stays: QNAP or UGREEN are the proven options, and the F6-425 Pro can only appear as a cheaper, maker-documented but unmeasured option.

findings.label: How the direct link works
findings.value: IP network over the cable: in TOS go to Control Panel > Network > Interface, 'locate the network interface starting with TBLAN, and set an IP address for it'. Put the computer's Thunderbolt network on the same subnet.
findings.note: The page says 'The USB4 / TB4 interface on TerraMaster NAS is compatible with Thunderbolt devices' but names no specific model.

findings.label: Host and cable requirement
findings.value: The computer needs a Thunderbolt 3/4/5 or full-featured USB4 port. Standard USB-C ports don't support direct connection, and the cable must be Thunderbolt 3/4/5 certified.
findings.note: The page also says 'macOS is recommended for better transfer efficiency' and that Windows may need drivers.

findings.label: Known caveat
findings.value: After either device restarts, the Thunderbolt interface's IP address may change and may need to be reconfigured.
findings.note: This is TerraMaster's own limitation note. Stability and performance depend on hardware, driver version and system environment.

findings.label: Reviewer status of the USB4 link
findings.value: Not yet measured. NASCompares lists 'Dual USB4 listed by TerraMaster' and says 'USB4 behaviour' is among items that 'all need proper review testing'.
findings.source_title: TerraMaster F6-425 Pro NAS – The Perfect Six-Bay Middle Ground for 10GbE and USB4? (NASCompares, 16 Jul 2026)
findings.note: A reader comment (25 Jul 2026, @studog858585) claims direct USB4 connection 'literally does not work'. It is unverified, so it is not used as a finding.

findings.label: Thunderbolt networking ceiling and Mac requirement
findings.value: Maximum bandwidth of 20 Gbps via Thunderbolt Networking. Works with Apple Silicon and Intel Macs. System requirement: macOS 13.5 or later.
findings.note: This was already cited by ChatGPT. The page doesn't name the Thunderbolt controller or say how many hosts can connect.

findings.label: Addressing
findings.value: Direct Mac connection needs IP configuration, and Qfinder Pro can assign the IP. Networking maximum 20Gb/s. The number of simultaneous users 'varies by model and the total number of ports'.
findings.note: This page was in ChatGPT's results but not cited.

findings.product: UGREEN NASync DXP480T Plus / DXP6800 Pro / DXP8800 Plus
findings.label: How the direct link works
findings.value: SMB over a dedicated Thunderbolt IP (169.254.x.x). One computer per port, and the two ports are not combined into a faster link. UGREEN: 'It does not give the computer direct control of the installed drives.' Plugging in the cable does not move an existing Ethernet-mapped share to Thunderbolt, so you must mount the Thunderbolt IP. Requires UGOS 1.2.0.2121 or later.
findings.source_title: How to Connect UGREEN NAS via Thunderbolt 4
findings.note: This was already cited by ChatGPT in one chat, so it is not new. Also says to keep the default MTU on both sides, and that sleep can drop the link.
